segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the Feuerbach Line is the line of centers of the incircle and the nine-point circle. By Karl Wilhelm Feuerbach's eighteen twenty-two theorem, the incircle and nine-point circle are internally tangent at the Feuerbach Point X eleven.

segments.text: Because the point of tangency of any two tangent circles lies on the line joining their centers, Incenter X one, Nine-Point Center X five, and Feuerbach Point X eleven are strictly collinear, with distance X one X five equal to R over two minus r.

segments.text: The external center of similitude of the incircle and nine-point circle is X twelve, which lies on the same Feuerbach line as the harmonic conjugate of X eleven with respect to X one and X five.
